turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. We will skip the weighing today, just the pressure. Sit straight and keep the arm relaxed.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister. I already took my watch off, because last time the cuff felt tight on this left arm and I don't want a wrong reading from that. I walked fast from the bus stop, though I am actually early, the traffic was on my mind the whole way.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Cuff reading is one forty-eight over ninety-two. Pulse is seventy-eight.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One forty-eight is higher than home, sister. This morning before tea my Omron showed one thirty-two over eighty-four, and I checked it twice. Maybe that fast walk pushed it up.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): I am writing one forty-eight over ninety-two, that is what this cuff showed. Doctor is free, you can go in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sit. What is the problem?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Two things, doctor, and I feel they are connected. The stomach is burning, and the sleep has become very bad. If I start with the stomach, the sleep will make more sense, unless you prefer the other way.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Where is the pain?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Centre, upper stomach, just below the breastbone. It is burning, like acidity, not a stabbing pain, and there is a little heaviness with it. Sometimes a sour taste comes up to the throat. It started after a heavy dinner at my cousin's place.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I was telling my wife three weeks, but if I think properly it is more like three to four weeks. It began after that dinner and then it just stayed. I keep rounding it off, but three to four weeks is the honest answer.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): All day?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): The burning comes and goes, but it has been there the whole three to four weeks. Evenings are worse, and if I lie down after dinner it flares up. In the shop, when I am talking to customers, I almost forget it is there.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting at all. One afternoon after biryani I felt nauseous, but nothing came up, and that was only once.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Black stool or blood?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I actually looked, because an uncle once had that and the whole family panicked. The colour is normal brown, and there is no blood.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight coming down?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, same weight. The belt hole is the same one I have used since last year.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sleep?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I lie down by eleven and I do fall asleep, then around two or sometimes three I am wide awake. The burning wakes me, and then the thoughts start, shop accounts, my son's college fees, and I cannot go back. This poor sleep has also been for a few weeks, the same period as the stomach. By four in the afternoon I am very tired.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you drink?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Only socially. With friends, that type of thing, nothing to worry about.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, a bottle of wine most nights, perhaps. Not every night, some nights I skip, but most nights yes. I said socially because it sounds better, I know. It is usually red wine, and I finish the bottle myself, I should not dress it up.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Smoke?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. Not even in college. My father smoked till the end and I hated the smell, so I never started.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): For the burning I take Crocin, one tablet, two or three times in a week, not daily. And for my BP I take the water tablet every morning. The proper name I cannot say, the chemist only writes water tablet on the cover.
[SEG0030] person_1 (NURSE): Sorry, doctor. His old slip says the water tablet is hydrochlorothiazide twenty-five milligrams once daily.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty-five? I don't think so, sister. The strip in my bathroom is twelve point five, and I take one tablet not two. My wife said the same, twelve point five, when she refilled it last month. Unless your slip is from before they changed the strength.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): You take it every day?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Daily, yes, morning, after brushing, that I never miss. The strength I will not swear to. I can bring the strip. I have had BP for about six years now, since the office medical in two thousand nineteen, roughly.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes tablets?

[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, sugar has been normal. No inhaler and no thyroid tablet. I do keep Gelusil liquid at home. I took it maybe twice this week when the burning was sharp, two spoons, not every day.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergy?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): None. I have had penicillin and I have had painkillers, no rash, no swelling, nothing like that ever.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any surgery before?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Appendix removed, nineteen ninety-eight or ninety-nine, at a mission hospital. I was in my twenties. No other operation, and the scar on the right side does not pain.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): In the family, ulcer or liver disease?

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Mother had acidity for years, she basically lived on Gelusil. Father had a liver problem, the doctors linked it to his drinking, and he died in twenty nineteen. My elder brother has nothing of this sort.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lie back. I am going to press on the stomach.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Soft. Mild tenderness in the upper middle. No guarding. Liver edge is not felt.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that spot is exactly where it burns when you press, the rest feels okay. I had coffee this morning, I hope that does not change what you are feeling. There was a loud parking argument in the corridor and it is still in my ear, sorry.

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Most likely acid-related, gastritis or reflux. The wine will be adding to the stomach and to the broken sleep. I am not here to scold you. We will check the liver with blood tests.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): You mean the liver is already bad, like my father? I should have said the wine in the first sentence, instead of going on about my cousin's dinner, I feel foolish now.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): I did not say the liver is damaged. It is a precaution. We will start a stomach medicine today.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pantoprazole forty milligrams, one every morning, half an hour before breakfast, for four weeks.

[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Before food, empty stomach, understood. And the Crocin, should I keep that for bad days? Sometimes Crocin is what I reach for, though the stomach is the real problem, not anything else.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the Crocin, you may not need it once the pantoprazole starts, and Gelusil if you need it is fine. Cut the wine right down, better none for these four weeks. No spicy food and no late dinner. Bring the water-tablet strip so we can settle the dose.

[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Liver function test today, sister will take you to the lab. See me in two weeks with the report. If you vomit blood or pass black stool, come earlier, do not wait for those two weeks.
